summary: TimeTagger is an open-source time tracking tool designed around an interactive timeline interface and detailed reporting capabilities. It allows you to record, categorise and analyse your working hours through a self-hosted web application. The codebase is written in Python and is distributed under the GNU General Public License v3.0.
goodFor: This is a suitable option if you want a self-hosted time-tracking utility with a focus on timeline visualization rather than complex billing workflows.
watchOut: The repository exhibits low maintenance activity and an at-risk health score, meaning you may encounter unpatched bugs or need to maintain the codebase yourself if issues arise.
deployNotes: As a Python application, you will typically need to run it behind a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination and configure persistent storage for your time-tracking database.
